assertions.name: control_support_is_four_two_row_blocks
assertions.source: convention D row cap: y_lambda = 0 for ell(lambda) > 2

assertions.name: cost_vanishes_on_kernel
assertions.source: t_l = y_l * chi^l, and y_l = 0 on the kernel

assertions.name: ame_exceeds_support_reachability_ceiling
assertions.source: t.x <= max(t)*n_target for x >= 0, sum x = n_target

description: Under convention D the deuteron operator-selection LP, restricted to the four supported (two-row) Wedderburn blocks with non-negative occupations, cannot reach the AME2020 binding: the objective is bounded by max(t)*n_target = 0.146058 against B_D = 2.224566, short by 15.2x. The full-space program met the AME value only because the seven zero-Gram kernel blocks carry no positivity constraint and so admit NEGATIVE occupations.
caveats: Scope (a). This bounds THIS cost vector on THIS program with non-negative occupations of the convention-D supported blocks. It does not refute any binding conjecture, does not say the encodings are wrong, and says nothing about a different cost, a different Wenzl level r, or a program that admits signed occupations for a stated reason.

The full-space numbers this replaces were not wrong arithmetic. They were the correct optimum of a program whose kernel is unconstrained, and the finding is that such a program does not mean what its field names suggest.
